In [[plasma physics]], an '''electrostatic ion cyclotron wave''' is a [[longitudinal wave|longitudinal]] oscillation of the [[ion]]s (and [[electron]]s) in a magnetized [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]], propagating nearly (but not exactly) perpendicular to the [[magnetic field]]. The angle (in [[radian]]s) between the direction of propagation and the direction perpendicular to the magnetic field must be greater than about the square root of the mass ratio,

:<math>\sqrt{\frac{m_e}{m_i}}</math>,

in order that the electrons can move along the field lines from crest to trough to satisfy the [[Boltzmann relation]]. The [[dispersion relation]] is
:<math>\omega^2=\Omega_c^2+k^2v_s^2</math>,<ref>{{cite book| author=Thomas Stix| author-link=Thomas H. Stix| title=The Theory of Plasma Waves | url=https://archive.org/details/theoryofplasmawa0000stix| url-access=registration| publisher = [[McGraw-Hill]] | year=1962}}</ref>
 
where Ω<sub>c</sub> is the ion [[cyclotron frequency]] and ''v''<sub>s</sub> is the [[ion acoustic wave|ion sound speed]]. This relation is the result of restoring forces due to the [[Lorentz force]] (see [[Upper hybrid oscillation]] for more details), the [[electrostatic force]] (the ''T''<sub>e</sub> term in ''v''<sub>s</sub>), and the ion pressure (the ''T''<sub>i</sub> term in ''v''<sub>s</sub>).
